summary: This is a Makefile that provides convenient commands for building and running a Docker container called 'dagger_daemon' with various development tools. Each target (build, bash, format, lint, etc.) either builds the Docker image or runs it with the necessary volume mounts to access Docker and the local source code.

explanations.1: DAEMON_NAME is a variable set to 'dagger_daemon' that's reused throughout the file, so if you need to change the container name, you only change it in one place.
explanations.2: DOCKER_SOCK is a variable storing the Docker socket mount command, which lets the container access Docker running on the host machine—this is necessary for the tools inside to build or manage containers.
explanations.4: .PHONY tells Make that 'build' is not a real file we're creating, so Make always runs this target even if a file named 'build' exists.
explanations.6: The docker build command constructs the Docker image using the Dockerfile in the .docker directory and tags it with the daemon name so we can reference it later.
explanations.10: docker run -it starts an interactive container with a terminal, --rm cleans it up after it exits, and --entrypoint /bin/bash opens a bash shell instead of running the default command.
explanations.14: This runs the format command inside the container by passing 'call format' as arguments, which presumably triggers code formatting in whatever tool the container uses.
explanations.30: docker rmi removes the Docker image itself (not just a running container), and --force deletes it even if it's still in use.
